# `05-position` — Position Engine

| | |
|---|---|
| **Tier** | T0 |

## Purpose

Position lifecycle and realized P&L: open, increase, decrease, reverse, close, hedge and net, with exact average-price and quantity accounting.

## Depends on

- [`04-account`](04-account.md) — Account Engine

## Depended on by

- [`08-pnl-margin`](08-pnl-margin.md) — P&L and Margin
- [`11-execution`](11-execution.md) — Execution Core
- [`19-client-api`](19-client-api.md) — Client API

## Inputs

- deals
- account state
- domain types

## Outputs

- Position
- realized P&L
- average price
- exposure per symbol

## What gets built

- netting and hedging position models (configurable per account)
- average price computation with declared rounding
- partial close, multi-fill aggregation, position reversal
- realized P&L posting into the ledger

## Invariants

These are executed as tests at gate **G4**. A module may not declare an
invariant it does not test.

- INV-040: quantity is conserved — sum(fills) == position delta, exactly.
- INV-041: every position mutation has exactly one originating event.
- INV-042: realized P&L on close equals the ledger postings for that close.
- INV-043: closing a position to zero leaves no residual quantity or residual average price.

## Test obligations

- property: random fill sequences conserve quantity and P&L
- partial closes summing to the full position equal one full close
- reversal through zero produces two positions, not one corrupt one

## Known failure modes

The things that go wrong in systems like this one. Each should map to a test above.

- average price drift from repeated rounding on partial fills
- reversal handled as a single signed mutation, losing the realized leg
